newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil testing $25.00 support.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil testing $25.00 support.

text.p: Singapore gas oil came under fresh selling pressure on lower crude prices and ample prompt supplies, traders said.
Traders said prices also came down because of the surplus prompt arbitrage cargoes totalling around 150,000 tonnes which is still seeking buyers.
As a result of the prompt pressure, the time spreads have narrowed sharply with May/June swaps now callled flat with June/June valued at 15 cents from over 60 cents on Monday, brokers said.
June gas oil swaps were last quoted at $24.90/$25.00 per barrel down sharply from Tuesday's $25.35/$25.45, brokers said.
In the physical market, two 150,000 barrel cargoes traded, one at $25.00 per barrel for May 29-June 2 lifting and the other at $25.10 for June 9-13 lifting, both on a free-on-board Singapore basis.
A European major and a Middle East trader sold the cargoes to a Singapore trader. The deals were between 20 to 30 cents below Tuesday's traded level, industry sources said.
Industry sources said Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has asked traders who had bid into its tender to sell 225,000 barrels of gas oil for June 4-17 lifting to revise their prices.
As a result of the request, CPC will award the tender on Thursday.

Jet fuel prices also fell in the wake of declining regional demand as the market moved to trade June barrels. A 100,000-barrel cargo traded between a European major and a Singapore trader at $24.80 per barrel for June 9-13 lifting, down 35 cents from Tuesday's traded level.
Taiwan's CPC issued a tender to buy July 1-30 cargoes after it skipped June due to high inventory.
